business_problem: Stellantis wanted to improve customer interactions, speed product-development analysis, and streamline manufacturing operations, but those goals required faster interpretation of component data, anomaly signals, fleet feedback, and driver support questions across a broad portfolio of vehicle models and brands.
solution_summary: Stellantis is using Mistral LLMs across several automotive workflows. Engineering teams are building a Bill of Materials Data Intelligence tool that analyzes component databases so they can identify, compare, and optimize part selections for global reuse. In parallel, Mistral technology is being evaluated for real-time anomaly detection on the manufacturing floor and for automated analysis of fleet feedback and survey data so teams can spot trends and corrective actions faster. Customer-facing experiences are part of the same architecture: a next-generation in-car assistant is being developed to answer natural-language questions about vehicle features, troubleshooting, and warning indicators, while the 'Club Stellantis' virtual assistant supports multilingual employee vehicle-purchasing workflows. The page does not name a separate storage tier, but it clearly describes shared analysis and assistant layers spanning engineering, factory, driver, and employee channels.
